findings.detail: The induction constructs genuine G walks between arbitrary specified branch endpoints. Each coarse edge adds one internal A walk of weight at most D and one real bridge of weight at most M; the base case adds the final internal walk, giving length(p)*(D+M)+D. Every component avoids the forbidden edge. The edge-local version propagates only membership in the current coarse walk and does not assume an external lifting oracle.

Weights are defined on Sym2 I, selecting a genuine B edge with the correct unordered pair of branch labels. Nonempty disjoint branches make labels faithful; the converse label lemma and orientation recovery return actual bridge endpoints in either requested orientation. This avoids an unsupported ordering or symmetric tie-breaking assumption. Coarse nonedge weights are zero but never used by the girth proof.

A selected dart decomposes the actual closed trail as prefix, selected edge, suffix. Concatenating suffix and prefix gives the correctly oriented endpoint-to-endpoint walk. Undirected edge-list nodup excludes the selected edge in either orientation. The theorem proves exact length(q)+1=length(p) and containment of every remaining edge; it does not merely postulate a shorter walk.

The maximum is taken over chosen bridge weights on the real finite quotient cycle. The removed coarse edge has a realizing host bridge of weight M>=L>0. Strict light/heavy separation excludes it from all internal walks; injectivity of unordered branch labels excludes it from bridges of the remaining coarse walk. The lift has the reverse endpoints needed by replacement_walk_gap. For m=length(p), the resulting inequality is g*M<m*(D+M). From m<=r, r*(1+D/L)<=g, D>=0 and M>=L>0, the proof obtains m*(D+M)<=r*(D+M)<=g*M, a contradiction. No simplicity assertion about the lifted walk, preserved greedy order, or global maximum over unrelated host edges is needed.

The quotient is genuinely a branch-set minor, so clique-minor exclusion transfers. The substitution D=d*ell and L=ell/(2*epsilon) is valid for positive ell and epsilon, giving D/L=2*d*epsilon. For k>=1, d>=0 and s>=4*d, the existing numerical repair gives 2*k*(1+2*d*epsilon)<=(1+s*epsilon)*(2*k-1)+1. This is exactly the required budget using corrected Claim 19, and proves actual quotient girth greater than 2*k.

limitations: ClusterFamily is explicitly supplied, including nonempty disjoint branches and internally supported diameter-bounded A walks. The final theorem assumes A<=G, B<=G, actual clique-minor exclusion and corrected intrinsic weighted girth, nonnegative host-edge weights, strict low-edge weights below L and heavy-edge weights at least L. It does not construct a multilevel hierarchy or derive these hypotheses from scale definitions.

The graph is the simple quotient with genuine crossing-edge witnesses. This checkpoint proves its cycle girth; complete transfer of all original heavy edges into a counting/charging argument still requires the relevant no-loop/uniqueness and coverage obligations.
The known Claim 19 threshold repair and strengthened sufficient parameter s>=4*d are correctly respected. No further mathematical correction was discovered.

Hierarchy existence, density increment/KT, asymptotic parameter selection and BLWN charging remain separate open obligations. No full-paper sparsity/lightness completion, exact-commit CI completion or publication approval is asserted.
